USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Celecoxib: 5

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient is scheduled for coronary artery bypass graft surgery and celecoxib is proposed for perioperative pain. Which labeling restriction specifically applies to this surgical setting, beyond the usual general review of NSAID risks?

  1. Reduced prostaglandin-supported renal perfusion
  2. Sodium and water retention
  3. Avoid use in the setting of CABG surgery
  4. Cyclooxygenase inhibition
  5. Gastrointestinal ulceration or bleeding
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Avoid use in the setting of CABG surgery

Celecoxib and other nonaspirin NSAIDs have a CABG-related contraindication in US labeling.

Understanding the options

Avoid use in the setting of CABG surgery
Celecoxib and other nonaspirin NSAIDs have a CABG-related contraindication in US labeling.
Cyclooxygenase inhibition
NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin synthesis by inhibiting cyclooxygenase enzymes. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Gastrointestinal ulceration or bleeding
Loss of protective mucosal prostaglandins contributes to NSAID-related ulceration and bleeding. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Reduced prostaglandin-supported renal perfusion
NSAIDs can impair afferent vasodilation, especially during volume depletion or reduced effective circulating volume. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Sodium and water retention
NSAIDs can cause fluid retention, worsen blood pressure and aggravate heart failure. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
